10.1002_anie.2221316: Renewable electricity‐driven electroreduction of CO 2 into formate represents one of the most commercially attractive routes for carbon valorization, yet Bi‐based catalysts often suffer from unstable surface states under reaction conditions. Here, we exploit this intrinsic instability to construct an interfacial Cs/Cl dual‐modified Bi nanoflower catalyst via an in situ electrochemical surface reconstruction strategy, which delivers high formate selectivity across a broad pH window, including acidic, neutral, and alkaline media. In situ spectroscopic analysis and theoretical calculations reveal that Cs/Cl dual‐modification fundamentally serves as synergistic sites by reconfiguring the interfacial electronic environment, accelerating water dissociation, and stabilizing *OCHO intermediates, thereby steering the reaction pathway toward formate. Furthermore, pairing CO 2 reduction with methanol oxidation in a two‐electrode configuration enables the simultaneous electrosynthesis of formate at both electrodes under low cell voltages, offering a dual‐value coproduction strategy for carbon utilization and biomass upgrading. This work establishes interfacial water activation via reconstruction‐induced dual‐sites as a powerful design principle for next‐generation CO 2 reduction electrocatalysts.
10.1016_j.jallcom.2026.190630: Borate-based glasses have attracted attention due to their tunable structural and functional properties. Herein, we present a systematic investigation of Ce 3+ -doped binary (Li 2 O-B 2 O 3 and MgO-B 2 O 3 ) and ternary (Li 2 O-MgO-B 2 O 3 ) borate glasses, establishing direct correlations among glass composition, structural evolution, defect formation, and photoelectrochemical response. Glasses were synthesized using the melt-quenching method and characterized by complementary structural, thermal, electrical, and luminescence techniques. XRD, FTIR, Raman, DSC, and EIS analyses indicated that variations in Li 2 O and MgO content modify the glass network connectivity and charge transport. Ce 3+ incorporation promoted a more homogeneous structural environment, as evidenced by smoother thermodynamic and optical signatures, and enhanced photoinduced charge-transport through defect-related states. OSL-C and OSL-P measurements confirmed the presence of efficient trapping centers associated with Ce 3+ , supporting a defect-mediated charge transport and recombination mechanism. These findings provide new insights into the combined role of Ce 3+ incorporation and glass composition in tailoring the photoelectrochemical properties of lithium-magnesium borate glasses, offering guidance for the design of advanced optoelectronic and photoactive materials.
10.1016_j.seppur.2025.135998: Ultrafiltration (UF) membranes based on Polyethersulfone (PES) are extensively used in food and bioprocessing industries for their mechanical robustness and chemical resistance. In starch and sweetener production, these membranes play a vital role in clarifying and purifying carbohydrate-rich syrups. However, sustaining membrane performance under industrial conditions, characterised by elevated temperatures, high pressures, and chemically complex feed solutions, remains a significant challenge due to fouling, membrane ageing, and irreversible performance loss. This study investigates the long-term performance of the GR90PP tight PES UF membrane (5kDa) from Alfa Laval, engineered for high-temperature (60-80 °C), high-pressure (beyond 5 bar) and chemical resistant applications, and certified for use in food processing environments due to its low protein adsorption. Experiments were conducted using a real starch hydrolysate syrup (DE40) to simulate industrial conditions. Performance was monitored over four filtration-cleaning cycles, focusing on flux behaviour, cleaning efficiency, solute rejection, and membrane integrity. Results showed a progressive Relative Flux Reduction (RFR), averaging 44 %, alongside a sigfinicant Flux Recovery Ratio (FRR) after cleaning, peaking at 80 % after the last alkaline rinsing. Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) analysis confirmed the gradual build-up of fouling layer, primarily organic in nature, contributing to reduced permeability and minor irreversible fouling (avg. 21 %). Alkaline cleaning proved significantly more effective than acidic cleaning, highlighting the dominance of organic fouling mechanisms. Overall, the GR90PP membrane demonstrated strong operational stability, chemical compatibility, and cleaning resilience, making it suitable for long-term and processing of carbohydrate-rich products. These findings underscore the importance of optimising cleaning protocols and operational parameters to sustain membrane performance in industrial food applications.
10.1016_j.seppur.2026.139238: Cold plasma is a promising electrified approach for wastewater treatment, but its performance in complex food-processing effluents is limited by matrix scavenging, foaming, and restricted plasma-liquid interactions. Here, we demonstrate a Fenton-integrated microbubble-enhanced cold plasma activation (MB-CPA) process for the purification of tofu-processing wastewater. Fenton pre-oxidation served as a priming step, reducing chemical oxygen demand (COD) by 32% and separation of suspended particles by 35%. The organic and protein-rich wastewater formed a persistent foamy suspension that intensified shielding, which was strategically destabilized by adding an antifoaming agent, restoring gas-liquid contact. In the subsequent MB-CPA stage, we varied the plasma discharge configurations, dual-needle corona discharge (56 W) versus dielectric barrier discharge (DBD, 100 W), to quantify their impact under identical microbubble-mediated gas delivery. Under corona discharge, MB-CPA reduced COD by 14.7%, decreased fat emulsions by 80%, and reduced total suspended solids by 53%. Switching to DBD increased mineralization efficiency by 2.3-fold relative to corona discharge, indicating that spatially extended plasma generation in DBD enhances oxidative treatment in quenching-prone wastewater matrices. Beyond pollutant removal, the treated effluent contained 372.8 μ M reactive nitrogen species and promoted plant growth, suggesting potential for nutrient valorization. Overall, the dual-stage strategy of Fenton priming and MB-CPA polishing demonstrates the potential of plasma-enabled oxidation to food-processing wastewater.
10.1021_acsami.5c23903: Understanding how chemical degradation influences proton transport in Nafion membranes is critical for improving the reliability of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). Here, we develop interpretable Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) frameworks to predict key transport properties, including vehicular and Grotthuss mechanism conductivities, and the tortuosity factor under varying water content, temperature, and degradation levels. Leveraging a high-fidelity, multiscale simulation data set, we trained a 3D convolutional neural network on voxelized membrane nanostructure data to predict proton conduction properties. Gradient-weighted class activation mapping is applied to highlight the spatial regions within the nanostructure that most strongly influence the predictions. We further develop random forest models based on extracted geometric features and macroscopic input conditions, with Shapley-value analysis used to quantify the impact of nanostructural and environmental factors. A fully coupled mechanism map is constructed to link hydration, temperature, and degradation with distinct conduction regimes. This visualization reveals how nanostructure aging reshapes proton conduction and provides a foundation for inverse design, which enables degradation-aware optimization of the membrane. Our study provides a multimodal AI framework capable of capturing both geometry and semantics in materials analysis and opens new avenues for predictive aging modeling and intelligent design in ion-conducting membranes.
10.1021_acsenergylett.6c02064: Magnesium (Mg) metal batteries are promising next-generation energy storage platforms, but practical deployment is hindered by the morphological instability and corrosion of the Mg metal anode during high-rate operation or extended rest. Here, we modulate the electronic work function (Φ) of Mg metal by controlling the electronic dipole in methoxy-amine solvents. Specifically, in situ incorporation of indium cations (In3+) into the electrolyte creates an interfacial dipole that elevates the Mg surface work function, mitigating parasitic corrosion inherent to methoxy-amine electrolytes. Simultaneously, the magnesiophilic In layer induces uniform hexagonal Mg growth and suppresses dendrite evolution. This electronic and chemical synergy achieves a Coulombic efficiency exceeding 98.5% at practical current densities, an eightfold longer reversibility, and extended calendar life across multiple solvents. In full cells with Mo6S8 cathodes, the system sustains over 1000 coin- and 300 pouch-cell cycles at 1C, demonstrating that interfacial electronic and nucleation control enables unprecedented lifetime stability for multivalent batteries.
10.1021_jacs.6c16802: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction offers a sustainable route for ammonia (NH3) synthesis, yet its efficiency is limited by sluggish N–O bond cleavage, incomplete NOx hydrogenation, and competing hydrogen evolution reaction. However, how catalyst structural engineering regulates the interfacial microenvironment remains unclear, despite its critical importance for constructing efficient catalysts. Here, we report a Cu3Ru7 catalyst with abundant Cu–Ru interfaces, where interface-induced water reorganization enables efficient NH3 production. The Cu3Ru7 catalyst exhibits an impressive NH3 formation rate of 19.7 mmol h–1 cm–2 at 5 A cm–2 in a membrane electrode assembly (MEA) electrolyzer and remains stable at 2 A cm–2 with an NH3 Faradaic efficiency of ∼86% for 500 h. A scale-up demonstration using a 100 cm2 MEA electrolyzer affords an NH3 formation rate up to 1.5 mol h–1 at 400 A. The in situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) reveals that Cu3Ru7 catalyst establishes a moderate interfacial hydrogen-bond network, which creates a water-mediated interfacial micro environment that facilitates NOx deoxygenation and subsequent NHx formation. Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations further reveal that the Cu–Ru interface stabilizes the dissociating oxygen atom through a persistent and dynamically connected hydrogen-bond network, thereby facilitating sequential NO3– → NO2 → NO conversion. Meanwhile, the surrounding Cu matrix attenuates the excessive *H accumulation characteristic of Ru, suppressing the hydrogen evolution reaction. This work establishes Cu–Ru interface-induced interfacial water reorganization as a strategy for improving electrocatalytic nitrate reduction performance.
10.1039_d5ta04819b: SFM-based single cells show high performance but poor long-term stability under steam electrolysis due to a dense interlayer formation at the SFM/GDC interface. In contrast, the cells with composite SFM-GDC electrodes exhibit exceptional durability.
10.1039_d6ta01370h: We investigate cyclohexylammonium salts with tailored alkyl chains in PSCs. Cyclohexylethylammonium iodide (CEAI) enables near-vertical orientation and strong defect interactions, yielding 25.58% efficiency (certified 25.30%) and enhanced stability.
10.1063_5.0305853: With the rapid development of wearable electronics and implantable medical devices, energy storage systems combining high-performance and biodegradability have attracted increasing attention. In this study, an oxide layer was in situ constructed on the surface of molybdenum (Mo) foil via high-temperature annealing, followed by uniform coating of ruthenium oxide (RuO2) nanoparticles, fabricating RuO2@MoOx heterostructure (HS). Furthermore, a quasi-solid-state biodegradable supercapacitor (SCs) was assembled with RuO2@MoOx HS as an electrode, achieving a specific capacitance of 544.6 F/g, along with an areal capacitance of 0.98 F/cm2 and a volumetric capacitance of 497.46 F/cm3 at 1 A/g. The device also exhibited an impressive cycle stability, retaining 85.9% of its capacitance after 2000 cycles, and an attractive energy density of 294.8 W h/kg at 987 W/kg. Moreover, the device underwent complete degradation in 5% hydrogen peroxide solution within 8 days, demonstrating excellent environmental responsiveness and biocompatibility. This work provides an effective strategy for the design and development of high-performance, biodegradable SCs and showcases promising application prospects in transient electronics and implantable biomedical systems.
